summary: Bound concurrent API read workers before opening SQLite readers, with cancellable admission and inline nested reductions

replay.detail: No claim, projection, or replay changes.

schema.detail: Admission is in-memory and does not alter the SQLite schema.

rules.detail: Read authority, snapshots, canonical answers, and durable write acknowledgements are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Each pool admits at most 32 top-level API read workers by default. Queued reads retain their existing cancellation and deadline behavior; upgraded-stream queries add no deadline policy. Same-pool nested reads reuse their loan; cross-pool nested reads try capacity without waiting, using an unadmitted nested loan when unavailable. Status fanout falls back inline. Collection gate waits hold no reader capacity, and a queued collection retains its FIFO reader grant into physical work.

downtime.detail: The setting takes effect when the daemon starts; no data migration is needed.

manual.detail: SMALLCLAIMS_MAX_READ_WORKERS overrides the positive admitted-worker count. Invalid, zero, or oversized values use 32. Idle reader retention, page-cache targets, statement caching, and allocator settings are unchanged; raw/background checkout and cross-pool nested fallback remain uncapped.

recovery.detail: Binary swap-back needs no migration and restores the previous unbounded API admission. Cancellation removes queued admission without opening a reader. A returned reader is cleaned up and published before its permit wakes another worker; escaped read guards retain capacity until the connection closes.
